gameTitle.text: A playful riff on SOURCE's name. Silently brainstorm 50 titles, then pick one with a real random number generator (e.g., run code).

package.text: For ease of deployment and sharing provide a single html file [GameTitle-SOURCE-{{model}}-{{effort}}-{{stamp}}.html]. Dependencies that can be downloaded do not have to be include in the html file if that is easier.

audio.text: Use code written Music and sound effects and Animalese / Simlish” / gibberish voice acting for any "voice" work.

workspace.text: Create a subfolder called [GameTitle-SOURCE-{{model}}-{{effort}}-{{stamp}}] here you can keep all your dev files. You can develop separate modules, then bundle into a single file [GameTitle-SOURCE-{{model}}-{{effort}}-{{stamp}}].html in root when the goal has been completed. You may use external CDN dependencies. Do not read files outside what you need - other agents share this directory.

performance.text: Treat it as unlimited. Add as much detail, enemies, effects, lights, and shadows as the scene needs. Out of scope (handled later): FPS targets, optimization.

research.text: Whether and how much to research is your choice.

premise.text: Build an original spiritual successor to {{source}}.

scope.text: Create a feature-complete demo inspired by {{source}}. Capture what makes the source distinctive while modernizing and improving its mechanics, pacing, and UX wherever it benefits the game. The demo must be long enough to show ALL features and gameplay mechanics so a player can clearly understand how the game plays and feels, and what they can and cannot do. Treat the demo as a complete, polished vertical slice / game engine. It should contain all the infrastructure, systems, and polish needed so the remainder of the game could later be built out with normal designer tools.

attractMode.text: After 10 seconds without input on the title/menu screen, start a looping AI-played demo or scripted replay (arcade/kiosk style); any input exits it. The AI (or replay) can be simple and may cheat freely (infinite health, ammo, abilities, no clip, etc). Its only job is to show as much of the demo as possible, the attract mode is not meant to balance the game.

multiplayer.text: Follow https://github.com/michaelcrosato/ai-hub/tree/main/lib/hub for multiplayer integration into ai-hub as well as for the game on its own.

tone.text: Use a writing style similar to the {{source}}.

uiux.text:
10-Foot Controller-First Philosophy
Design all interfaces and interactions for a "10-foot experience" with a PS5-compatible controller as the primary input. Keyboard and mouse are secondary inputs that map to the controller's interaction model, not a separate desktop paradigm. Apply modern UX principles. Use your judgment to balance deep systemic information with clean, uncluttered presentation.

Common Issue (~10%): Gamepad horizontal/vertical input is intermittently inverted. As a quick fix, add toggles in Settings to invert horizontal and vertical axes.

Do not use overly dense, web-style data screens.

Touch-only devices: no touch controls; show "Controller or keyboard required" and the settings button.

done.text: No TODOs, placeholders, or stubbed features. The demo is complete.

sourceInfo.text:
CRTICAL: Put Source Information, Engine Feedback and Prompt Feedback in your chat reply, an in-game About/Credits screen, and an HTML comment at the top of the file. Write "unknown" for anything you can't confirm.
- Date: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
- {{source}}
- Genre and Perspective: genre and camera perspective used
- Tech: stack, libraries/engines, with versions if applicable
- Art Direction: style used
- Animation: system used
- Audio: music, sound effects and voice used
- Online: network features used, or none
- Testing: testing parameters allowed
- Research: research done, or none
- Environment: {{environment}}
- Model: {{lab}}, {{model}}, reasoning effort {{effort}}
- Usage: the estimated API cost in USD, total number of tokens in K or M  (provide break down if available) and session time, only if estimates are available.

testingFeedback.text:
- How many issues did testing catch?
- How many would be considered critical issues / game breaking?
- What was the most helpful test you ran?
- What was the least helpful test you ran?

engineFeedback.text:
- What did you like most about the engine?
- Did you get stuck or guess wrong?
- What was the most important thing you had to build yourself?
- What was the hardest part about using the engine?
- If you had to remove or overhaul one thing from engine, what woudl that be?
- If you could change one thing about the engine, what would it be?

promptFeedback.text:
- What did you like most about this prompt?
- What was confusing? 
- What was the hardest thing to do? 
- If there was one test you could of run, what would that test be?

goal.text: the bundled single .html file exists in this folder's root, every feature in TASK.md is implemented with no TODOs, placeholders or stubs, and your final reply contains the Source Information, Engine Feedback and Prompt Feedback sections.

stages.text: Read TASK.md in this folder: it describes a game to build. Don't build it yet: plan it. Write PLAN.md in this folder for the developers who will build it from TASK.md and your plan; they may be other AI models, working without you. Start PLAN.md with the game's title, picked as TASK.md says. Cover the architecture and modules, every system and mechanic TASK.md asks for, the content (levels, enemies, items, story beats), the order to build in with milestones, the riskiest parts and how to de-risk them, and how to test each part. Be specific enough that a capable developer can build the whole demo from TASK.md and PLAN.md alone. Then reply with a short summary of the plan.
stages.goal: PLAN.md exists in this folder and covers the title, architecture, every system, the content, the build order and testing for everything TASK.md asks for.

stages.text: Read TASK.md (what to build) and PLAN.md (how to build it, written by {{parentModel}} at {{parentEffort}} effort) in this folder. Build the game TASK.md describes, following the plan and using the title it gives; where they disagree, TASK.md wins. Deliver everything TASK.md asks for, including its file name, and the sections it asks for in your final reply.
stages.goal: the bundled single .html file exists in this folder's root, every feature in TASK.md is implemented with no TODOs, placeholders or stubs, and your final reply contains the Source Information, Engine Feedback and Prompt Feedback sections.

stages.text: The game in this folder was built from TASK.md and PLAN.md; the steps so far: {{chain}}. Its framework is done. Your job is content and polish on top of it: more of what TASK.md asks for (levels, enemies, items, quests, music, effects, story) and fixes for anything broken. Keep the game's title, engine and architecture, and extend them rather than starting over. Save the result as a new bundled single .html in this folder's root, named as TASK.md says but with the game's current title, and in your final reply list what you added and give the sections TASK.md asks for.
stages.goal: a new bundled single .html with the added content exists in this folder's root, nothing that worked before is broken, and your final reply lists what you added and contains the Source Information, Engine Feedback and Prompt Feedback sections.
